Flux2ImageNode/Flux.2 [pro].label: FLUX.2 [pro]

price.basis: one image up to 1 megapixel; add 3.17 credits ($0.015) per whole extra megapixel

Flux2ImageNode/Flux.2 [pro].strengths: Production text to image with hex-code colour control
Flux2ImageNode/Flux.2 [pro].notes: The node's width and height are free integers, so the size is not a preset list: clamp to 256-2048 in steps of 32. BFL documents up to 4 MP output; 2048x2048 is 4.19 MP, so the node's own max is the binding limit. Cost rises with output megapixels, which is unusual among image models and should be visible in the size control. No documented prompt length limit on either side.

Flux2ImageNode/Flux.2 [max].label: FLUX.2 [max]

price.basis: one image up to 1 megapixel; add 6.33 credits ($0.03) per whole extra megapixel

Flux2ImageNode/Flux.2 [max].strengths: Highest quality FLUX.2, with web grounding for real-world facts
Flux2ImageNode/Flux.2 [max].notes: Same node and same size rules as Flux.2 [pro], at 2.3x the price. BFL documents grounding search on [max] only: it can look up real-time facts when the prompt asks for them. A 2048x2048 image is 4 megapixels and costs 33.76 credits, not 14.77.

FluxProUltraImageNode.label: FLUX 1.1 [pro] Ultra

constraints.note: The ratio has to be between 1:4 and 4:1.

price.basis: flat, every aspect ratio

FluxProUltraImageNode.strengths: 4 megapixel output at one flat price, with a raw photographic mode
FluxProUltraImageNode.notes: Output is always about 4 MP; there is no size control, only an aspect ratio typed as a free string (default 16:9). The `raw` boolean is a real capability, not a style preset: BFL documents it as candid-photography output with more subject diversity. BFL's own price is $0.06 and Comfy resells at cost. There is no resolution or size input on this node at all: the output is always about 4 MP and only the aspect ratio can be set, so the form must not draw a size control.

FluxKontextProImageNode.label: FLUX.1 Kontext [pro]

constraints.note: The ratio has to be between 3:7 and 7:3. A wider one is sent but refused.

price.basis: flat

FluxKontextProImageNode.notes: Kontext is primarily an image editing model; text to image works because `input_image` is optional. BFL now recommends FLUX.2 for new text-to-image work. All outputs are about 1 MP, 1024x1024 at 1:1. This node has no price badge in the ComfyUI source, so the price comes from the Comfy pricing page and BFL's own table, which agree exactly. There is no resolution or size input on this node at all: the output is always about 1 MP and only the aspect ratio can be set, so the form must not draw a size control.

FluxKontextMaxImageNode.label: FLUX.1 Kontext [max]

constraints.note: The ratio has to be between 3:7 and 7:3. A wider one is sent but refused.

price.basis: flat

FluxKontextMaxImageNode.strengths: Kontext at maximum quality, best for typography
FluxKontextMaxImageNode.notes: Kontext is primarily an image editing model; text to image works because `input_image` is optional. BFL now recommends FLUX.2 for new text-to-image work. Flux3TextToVideoNode.label: FLUX 3 Text to Video

price.basis: 720p; audio is included at no extra charge

Flux3TextToVideoNode.strengths: Long clips, up to 20 s, with synchronised speech and ambience
Flux3TextToVideoNode.notes: Expensive: a 10 s 1080p clip is 875 credits, about $4.15. `duration` may be the string 'auto', in which case the total cannot be estimated in advance, only the per-second rate; the picker should say so. BFL documents a `draft` mode that renders at hd for about a third of the price, and the ComfyUI node does not expose it, so the cheap preview path is unavailable here. `safety_tolerance` 0 to 4 is an extra with a schema default of 2.

IdeogramV4.label: Ideogram 4.0

price.basis: rendering_speed DEFAULT

IdeogramV4.strengths: Literal text rendering, and structured JSON prompts for exact layout
IdeogramV4.notes: One image per run: Ideogram's V4 endpoint has no num_images field, so no batch. `rendering_speed` is the price control and belongs beside the price, not buried in More options. The node exposes only the 2K-class sizes plus Auto; Ideogram's API also offers 1024x1024, 1280x720, 512x1536 and 14 other smaller sizes that this node cannot reach, and it does not offer FLASH or BALANCED rendering speeds. Ideogram documents that negative prompts are unnecessary on 4.0 and the node has no negative prompt input.

IdeogramV3.label: Ideogram 3.0

constraints.note: The ratio is ignored once a size is named: the size decides the shape.

price.basis: rendering_speed DEFAULT, multiplied by num_images

IdeogramV3.strengths: Up to 8 images per run, with a real negative prompt
IdeogramV3.notes: Ideogram V3 has no row on the Comfy pricing page at all; these figures come from the node's own price_badge, which is the same source the pricing page is written from for every other Ideogram row. Note that V3 QUALITY (27.16 credits) is cheaper than V4 QUALITY (30.17). Attaching a character_image roughly triples the price (turbo 30.17, default 45.26, quality 60.35 credits per image), but that input is out of scope for text to image. Ideogram's API also offers FLASH and BALANCED rendering speeds that the node does not expose.

IdeogramPImage.label: Ideogram P-Image

price.basis: quality MEDIUM at 1K; 2K is exactly double at every tier

IdeogramPImage.strengths: Ideogram's budget tier, 0.91 credits at 1K on the lowest quality setting
IdeogramPImage.notes: At 0.91 credits a 1K VERY_LOW image is about a tenth of a Seedream 5.0 Pro image, which makes P-Image the right default for drafts and for any automated batch. The node's own tooltip warns that text renders poorly below MEDIUM. The node outputs (IMAGE, STRING); the STRING is the rewritten final_prompt, which is how a run is reproduced: reuse it with prompt_upsampling OFF and the same seed. Ideogram's API has a VERY_HIGH quality tier and custom_width/custom_height that the node does not expose.

KlingImageGenerationNode/kling-v3.label: Kling 3.0 Image

price.basis: per image, multiplied by n (1 to 9)

KlingImageGenerationNode/kling-v3.strengths: Nine images a run at 5.91 credits each, with native text rendering
KlingImageGenerationNode/kling-v3.notes: `negative_prompt` is a required STRING on this node, so the builder must always send it, empty if unused. `image_type`, `image_fidelity` and `human_fidelity` are required but only matter when a reference image is attached; keep their schema defaults. No output size control at all, only an aspect ratio.

KlingOmniProImageNode/kling-v3-omni.label: Kling 3.0 Omni Image

price.basis: 1K or 2K, multiplied by series_amount

KlingOmniProImageNode/kling-v3-omni.strengths: 4K output, and a series of up to nine consistent images in one run
KlingOmniProImageNode/kling-v3-omni.notes: 2K costs the same as 1K, which is worth telling the user in the size control. Batch is spelled `series_amount` and its values are the strings 'disabled','2'..'9', not an integer. The prompt takes both positive and negative description in one field; there is no separate negative prompt.

KlingOmniProImageNode/kling-image-o1.label: Kling Image O1

constraints.note: Kling Image O1 has no 4K: it makes 1K and 2K images.
Kling Image O1 makes one image per run, never a series.

price.basis: flat at 1K and 2K

KlingOmniProImageNode/kling-image-o1.strengths: Kling's reasoning image model, one image at a time
KlingOmniProImageNode/kling-image-o1.notes: Shares a node with kling-v3-omni, so the schema offers 4K and series_amount for it; both are refused at execute time. That is the clearest example in this vendor set of why the picker must carry constraints rather than trust the combo lists.

KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode/kling-v3-omn.label: Kling 3.0 Omni Text to Video

price.basis: 720p, audio off

KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode/kling-v3-omn.strengths: 4K video with multilingual dialogue and lip sync
KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode/kling-v3-omn.notes: 4K is five times the 1080p rate: a 5 s 4K clip is 443 credits, about $2.10. Audio is free at 4K and adds a third at 720p and 1080p. The `storyboards` dynamic combo (up to six segments, each with its own prompt and duration) is a real multi-shot feature; the node requires the segment durations to sum to the global `duration`, and each segment prompt is capped at 512 characters. Treat storyboards as an extra, not a role.

KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode/kling-video-.label: Kling Video O1

constraints.note: Kling Video O1 makes 5 and 10 second clips only.
Kling Video O1 has no sound.
Kling Video O1 has no 4K: it tops out at 1080p.
Kling Video O1 does not take storyboards.

KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode/kling-video-.strengths: Kling's reasoning video model at the plain 720p rate
KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode/kling-video-.notes: Four hard constraints that the node schema does not express: duration, audio, 4k and storyboards are all rejected at execute time. This entry is the strongest argument in the vendor set for machine-usable constraints in the picker.

KlingVideoNode/kling-v3.label: Kling 3.0 Video

price.basis: 720p, audio off

KlingVideoNode/kling-v3.strengths: Multi-shot video with locked subject identity across shots

They live inside the `multi_shot` dynamic combo under its 'disabled' key (multi_shot.prompt, multi_shot.negative_prompt, multi_shot.duration), and the resolution and aspect live inside the `model` combo. A role mapper that only looks at top-level inputs will mark this node unsupported. Audio costs 50 percent more at 720p and 1080p and nothing at 4K.

KlingVideoNode/kling-3.0-turbo.label: Kling 3.0 Turbo Video

constraints.note: Kling 3.0 Turbo always comes with sound, at the same price, and it cannot be turned off.

price.basis: 720p, audio always included

KlingVideoNode/kling-3.0-turbo.strengths: Faster Kling 3.0 with audio always on
KlingVideoNode/kling-3.0-turbo.notes: No 4K on turbo. Same nested-input structure as kling-v3 on this node: prompt and duration live under `multi_shot`. Turbo is dearer than kling-v3 with audio off and cheaper than kling-v3 with audio on, so 'cheapest' sorting has to know whether sound is wanted.

KlingTextToVideoWithAudio/kling-v2-6.label: Kling 2.6 Text to Video with Audio

price.basis: audio off; audio exactly doubles the rate

KlingTextToVideoWithAudio/kling-v2-6.notes: No resolution control at all, so the picker's capability line should say 'no size choice'. Audio doubles the price, which is the single largest audio surcharge in this vendor set and must be visible at the click.

KlingTextToVideoNode.label: Kling 2.5 Turbo Text to Video

PixverseTextToVideoNode.label: PixVerse v3.5

PixverseTextToVideoNode.notes: PRICE MISMATCH, the only one in this vendor set. The Comfy pricing page lists 94.95, 126.6, 189.9 and 253.2 credits for these shapes; the node's own price_badge lists USD figures that are exactly 1.43 times higher (Comfy's usual reseller markup), which is what is recorded above. RecraftV4TextToImageNode/recraftv4_pro.notes: The `negative_prompt` input exists but the node's own tooltip says it is ignored on V4 and V4.1: do not offer it. Every size costs the same within a model, and the Pro variants differ from the base ones only by size list and price (2048-class against 1024-class). Recraft's published per-image prices match Comfy's exactly, so Comfy resells Recraft at cost. Prompt limit 10000 characters, enforced by the node. Attaching style_references adds 1.06 credits ($0.005) per run, but that needs images and is out of scope here.

RunwayTextToImageNode.label: Runway Gen-4 Image

price.basis: flat, every ratio

RunwayTextToImageNode.strengths: Runway's Gen-4 look, with reference-image support
RunwayTextToImageNode.notes: Sizes are written with a colon, '1920:1080', not an 'x', and they are exact pixel sizes rather than aspect ratios: parse them as a sizePreset. Runway's own API accepts sixteen ratios for gen4_image; the ComfyUI node exposes only these ten, missing 1280:720, 720:1280, 720:720, 960:720, 720:960 and 1680:720. The node has no seed input at all. Runway charges 5 credits for a 720p image and 8 for 1080p at $0.01 a Runway credit; Comfy bills a flat 24.14 credits ($0.1144), which is 1.43 times Runway's 1080p rate, so a small image costs the same as a large one here. Small discrepancy worth knowing: the node's own price badge says $0.11 while the Comfy pricing page says 24.14 credits ($0.1144); the page figure is recorded. The model id above is what the node sends upstream; it is NOT a selectable input on this node, so the builder must not try to write a `model` field.

Vidu3TextToVideoNode/viduq3-turbo.label: Vidu Q3 Turbo

price.basis: 720p; audio does not change the rate

Vidu3TextToVideoNode/viduq3-turbo.strengths: Vidu's fast tier with audio at no extra charge, clips to 16 s
Vidu3TextToVideoNode/viduq3-turbo.notes: Audio, including dialogue and sound effects, is a free boolean on Q3. Up to 16 s in one clip. Vidu's Q3 API also has a 540p tier and a 2K tier; the ComfyUI text-to-video node offers neither (2K is documented as image-to-video with viduq3-pro only), so 720p is the floor here. Prompt limit 2000 characters, enforced by the node. STRUCTURAL WARNING: aspect_ratio, resolution, duration and audio live inside the `model` dynamic combo while the prompt stays at the top level.

Vidu3TextToVideoNode/viduq3-pro.label: Vidu Q3 Pro

price.basis: 720p; audio does not change the rate

Vidu3TextToVideoNode/viduq3-pro.strengths: Vidu's quality tier, with free audio and clips to 16 s
Vidu3TextToVideoNode/viduq3-pro.notes: Two and a half times the turbo rate at 720p but only twice at 1080p, so 1080p pro is relatively better value than 720p pro. The Comfy pricing page lists a 2K tier for viduq3-pro at 42.2 credits a second, but it says explicitly that 2K exists only on the image-to-video node, and the text-to-video node's resolution combo confirms this by offering only 720p and 1080p.

Vidu2TextToVideoNode/viduq2.label: Vidu Q2

price.basis: 720p base for the first second, then 5.275 credits ($0.025) per further second

Vidu2TextToVideoNode/viduq2.strengths: A base-plus-per-second rate, so long clips get cheaper per second
Vidu2TextToVideoNode/viduq2.notes: The only pricing shape in this vendor set that is not flat per run or flat per second: a base for the first second and a lower rate after it. A 10 s 720p clip is 63.3 credits, which is cheaper per second than any other video model here. The audio control is spelled `background_music` and only adds music, not dialogue; Q3's `audio` is the fuller feature. Prompt limit 2000 characters.

ViduTextToVideoNode/viduq1.label: Vidu Q1

constraints.note: One size and one length: 5 seconds at 1080p.

price.basis: flat, the only shape

ViduTextToVideoNode/viduq1.strengths: Vidu's previous generation, one fixed 5 s 1080p clip
ViduTextToVideoNode/viduq1.notes: No choices at all beyond aspect ratio and movement amplitude: duration is pinned to 5 and the resolution combo has one option. At 84.4 credits it costs exactly the same as five seconds of Vidu Q3 Turbo at 1080p (16.88 a second), and half what five seconds of Vidu Q3 Pro at 1080p costs. Q3 Turbo gives audio and a length choice for the same money, so Q1 has no reason to be recommended.

MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode/MiniMax H.notes: Added to ComfyUI 0.34.4 as the fast tier of H3 Max, and it shares the Max code path: the same /proxy/fal/minimax/h3-max-turbo endpoint style, the same 50000 character prompt limit, the same 5 to 15 second slider and the same refusal of a watermark, which the node raises as "Watermark is only supported by MiniMax H3." Comfy's H3 tutorial independently calls Turbo about half the Max rate, and half of Max is exactly these two figures, so two sources agree. Audio is recorded the same way as H3 and H3 Max: the node declares no sound input at all, so there is nothing to switch and nothing extra to pay for. `prompt_expansion_mode` (balanced or quality) is a required extra, as on Max. At 480P, 0.03575 dollars a second is 7.54325 credits, so a 5 second clip is 37.72 credits.

MetaMuseImageTextToImageApi/muse-image-1.label: Muse Image 1.0

capabilities.outputSize: about 2.5 megapixels at every ratio: 1600x1600 at 1:1, 2048x1152 at 16:9; no size control

The two agree to the cent, so the figure is recorded at the usual two decimals as 3.02. The tooltip promises 1600x1600 at 1:1.

MetaMuseImageTextToImageApi/muse-image-1.strengths: Plans and self-refines before it renders, and can search the web while it plans
MetaMuseImageTextToImageApi/muse-image-1.notes: New in the 2026-09-08 catalog. Everything lives inside the `model` dynamic combo, so the wire names are `model.prompt`, `model.aspect_ratio` and so on. There is no size or resolution control at all: aspect ratio is the only geometry input and the model renders every ratio at about 2.5 megapixels. `reasoning_strength` (high or low) changes how long it thinks, and the three advanced booleans (`enable_web_search`, `enable_image_search`, `enable_shell`) let it look things up and run code while planning; all three default to on and none of them changes the price. The seed input is decorative: the node's own tooltip says the API has no seed and results are nondeterministic regardless. The sibling MetaMuseImageEditApi is the same model behind an edit node that demands one to ten input images, so it is not a text to image model and is recorded as unsupported by the generator.

The figures here are computed from that expression at a 200 character prompt, and the range covers every ratio, because 4:3 is 768 output tokens against 1024 at 1:1. The prompt is about half a percent of the total, so a long one barely moves it. A reference image adds its own tokens on top, which estimateCredits does not model.

price.note: 7.24 credits an image at 1K and 2K, 9.66 at 4K, which is a 2K render upscaled by the model. From the node's own price badge (0.03432 and 0.04576 US dollars, times 211), and the 7.24 agrees with the pricing row Comfy's docs added for this model. HunyuanImageTextToImageApi/hy-image-3.5-.strengths: Multilingual text and typesetting for posters and infographics, 1K to 4K
HunyuanImageTextToImageApi/hy-image-3.5-.notes: New in the 2026-09-24 catalog (ComfyUI 0.37.1, 2026-09-22). Everything lives inside the model dynamic combo, so the wire names are model.prompt, model.aspect_ratio, model.resolution, model.width, model.height, model.seed and model.watermark. The resolution list also carries 'custom', which reads model.width and model.height (multiples of 16, up to 4096x4096 in area); the plugin drops Custom as it does everywhere and sizes by ratio and tier, and the builder still sends the node's default 2048x2048 because both inputs are required. Tencent documents 2K as the native size: 4K is rendered at 2K and upscaled. 'auto' lets the model pick the ratio from the prompt and the node refuses it at 4K. The model rewrites and expands the prompt before rendering, and the seed tooltip says results still vary between runs with the same seed. The sibling HunyuanImageEditApi is the same model behind an edit node that demands one to five reference images, so it is unsupported. This text to image node takes no reference image at all.

PrunaTextToVideoNode/p-video-2.label: P-Video-2

constraints.note: A draft at 1080p only renders at 24 frames a second.

price.note: Per second of output: 7.54 credits at 720p and 15.09 at 1080p, and a draft is 60 percent of that, 4.53 and 9.05. The node's price badge (0.03575, 0.0715, 0.02145 and 0.0429 US dollars, times 211) and Comfy's pricing page agree to the cent. Sound and frame rate do not change the price. On 'auto' length the badge shows only the rate, and this plugin gives no figure.

PrunaTextToVideoNode/p-video-2.strengths: Clips of 1 to 20 seconds with native sound, and a draft mode at 60 percent of the price
PrunaTextToVideoNode/p-video-2.notes: New in the 2026-09-24 catalog (ComfyUI 0.36.0, 2026-09-15). Everything lives inside the model dynamic combo. Duration is a combo of 'auto' plus the strings '1' to '20', with a default of '5'; the plugin offers the numbers and not 'auto', because on 'auto' the model picks any length from 1 to 20 seconds from the prompt and a per second price then has no figure, so a graph sent through run_workflow with 'auto' is refused a quote rather than quoted at five seconds. fps is '24' or '48' and is sent as a string, since the catalog spells it that way. draft bills 60 percent of the standard rate and cannot be combined with 48 fps at 1080p. generate_audio defaults to on in the node and costs nothing extra; the plugin's own form starts it off, as it does for every model. enhance_prompt (on by default) rewrites the prompt before generating, and only with it off does the same seed reproduce a result. 720p renders 1280x704 and 1080p 1920x1088 at 16:9. The optional audio input, which would set the length itself, is not wired. The sibling PrunaImageToVideoNode needs a first frame and is unsupported.
